Senses.Explanation: This stock closing challenge asks an interlocutor or assembly whether they understand: “do you get it?” Chan records use it after statements, gestures, verses, and raised cases to demand a response rather than merely close a paragraph. The dominant frame is "do you still get it?" (還會麼; 2085 occ / 270 texts); it is addressed to the assembly as (大眾會麼) (261) and (諸人會麼) (48). The recurring pattern presents a saying, raised case, held-up object, or abrupt action and then asks (還會麼); the question is frequently followed by (良久) (a pause) and a further line, e.g. (還會麼良久云三邊若得渾無事) and (召大眾云還會麼良久擲如意云); or the interlocutor answers "I don't get it" (不會), e.g. (陛下還會麼)。(帝曰)。(不會) and (拈起帽子兩帶曰)。(還會麼)。(曰)。(不會). In a public encounter Xingkong Xingzhen overturns the dining table, asks (會麼), and judges the lecturer's answer "table"; Yunmen Wenyan sharpens the same question to (驢年會麼), "will you get it in the year of the donkey?" It also stands as the pivot before a verdict — "do you get it? if not yet…" (諸人還會麼。其或未然) — and closes an address, (良久曰)：(還會麼)？(珍重). The texts use it as a discourse marker and assign it no further gloss, and neither does this entry.
Senses.Note: One corpus-wide discourse marker. The curated occurrences name Shanhui Dashi, Guizong Zhichang, Hongzhi Zhengjue, Yunfeng, Tianyi Yihuai, Yulin Tongxiu, Yunmen Wenyan, Xingkong Xingzhen, and Jing'an Che as the questioners. Yunmen Wenyan's marked (驢年會麼) remains the same understand-question and belongs to the corpus-wide usage rather than a private usage. The reciprocal reply in the record is (不會). Counts: (會麼) 6053/367; (還會麼) 2085/270; (大眾會麼) 261; (諸人會麼) 48.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Five Lamps Meeting at the Source (五燈會元), section on Shanhui Dashi: Shanhui Dashi puts the challenge to the emperor, drawing the stock reply 'I do not get it.' Shanhui Dashi is source-attested but not yet in the roster.

Occurrences.Kwic: 乃拈起帽子兩帶曰。還會麼。曰。不會。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Five Lamps Meeting at the Source (五燈會元), section on Guizong Zhichang: Guizong Zhichang raises a hat's two ties, asks whether the monk gets it, and receives 'I do not get it.'
The Extended Record of Chan Master Hongzhi (宏智禪師廣錄): Hongzhi Zhengjue uses the assembly-address form 'do all of you still get it?' as the pivot to 'if not yet so.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 諸禪德還會麼良久云三邊若得渾無事
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Old Recorded Sayings of Venerable Masters (古尊宿語錄), section headed 'Chan Master Yunfeng': Yunfeng asks whether the Chan worthies get it, pauses, and follows with a couplet. Yunfeng is source-attested but not yet in the roster.
The Complete Collection of the Five Lamps, volumes 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), section on Tianyi Yihuai: Tianyi Yihuai pauses, asks whether the assembly gets it, and dismisses them with 'take care.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 召大眾云還會麼良久擲如意云
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Recorded Sayings of National Master Puji Yulin (普濟玉琳國師語錄): Yulin Tongxiu summons the assembly, asks whether they get it, pauses, and throws down the ceremonial scepter.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師云：「我今日不荅話。」進云：「為什麼不答話？」師云：「驢年會麼？」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yunmen Kuangzhen (雲門匡真禪師語錄): after refusing to answer, Yunmen Wenyan replies to 'why?' with the sharpened challenge 'Will you get it in the year of the donkey?' This remains the same understand-question, not another sense.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師掀飯床，云：「會麼？」主云：「桌子。」師云：「須知老僧好手。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Xingkong Zhen (性空臻禪師語錄): Xingkong Xingzhen overturns the dining table and asks 'Do you get it?' The lecturer answers 'table,' and Xingkong gives his verdict. Xingkong Xingzhen is source-attested but not yet in the roster.

Occurrences.Kwic: 大眾會麼普大眾不會麼庭前栢樹子
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Recorded Sayings of National Master Puji Yulin (普濟玉琳國師語錄): Yulin Tongxiu asks whether the assembly gets it and, anticipating that it does not, answers with the cypress tree in the courtyard.

Occurrences.Kwic: 諸人會麼？名不得、狀不得、取不得、舍不得，嘗照嘗現
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Complete Collection of the Five Lamps, volumes 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), section on Jing'an Che: Jing'an Che asks whether all of them get it, then says it cannot be named, described, taken, or discarded. Jing'an Che is source-attested but not yet in the roster.
